name: Chain of Strength
label: Revelation
lede: Two seven-inches, about three years, a demo tape that got signed in a parking lot, and a logo that hardcore kids have been redrawing on their own shirts ever since.

eras.title: Signed from a car stereo
eras.text: Southern California straight edge was mostly borrowing its look and sound from Boston and New York. Chain of Strength wanted the heft of the Cro-Mags with the melody of Dag Nasty, and before they'd finished their first show, Ray Cappo had asked to put them on Revelation.

years.h: Chain of Strength's plan: [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]] power, [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]] melody
years.p: Curtis Canales sings, Frosty (Paul Hertz) and [[Ryan Hoffman|22c60d75-ef91-4601-8467-2fd06b67842d]] play guitar, Alex Barreto plays bass and [[Chris Bratton|cbaf85ca-1bc7-4eb0-b9cb-ca5d8773b27f]] plays drums. The sound Frosty wanted: Cro-Mags heft, Dag Nasty melody.
years.xp: Bratton came in fresh from [[No for an Answer|23d26104-95e2-473f-a704-ab0bcd702da3]] and [[Justice League|550a452b-26f6-4ba8-993d-7b8fbf1f691f]].

years.src: RevHQ Speak Up: Ryan Hoffman · No Echo
years.h: Chain of Strength's first show, and Ray Cappo hears their demo
years.p: Ryan Hoffman and a friend booked the show themselves, with Chain of Strength opening. [[Ray Cappo|e8357f9d-f7f5-4858-a766-aef004bb38a6]] heard the band's demo in Hoffman's car and asked for it on Revelation.
years.xp:
The bill: [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Insted|3677d0cb-dd2e-472e-b92b-f64cec75ddb4]], [[Underdog|de38fbd3-7155-497a-bf3c-1a8db3091859]], [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]], [[Hard Stance|3029fc29-bf7c-4f78-8bfc-97c0bf144c6d]], [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]], and a brand-new Chain of Strength on the bottom. Cappo told Hoffman on the spot he wanted the tape, and Hoffman said yes on the spot too.

Hoffman has said what made that day last wasn't the offer. It was the do-it-yourself show and the friendships, the San Diego crew among them, that started in that room.

years.h: Chain of Strength's East Coast debut at the Anthrax
years.p: The Connecticut club, on a bill with [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]] and [[Alone in a Crowd|1639f026-7a51-4762-a3f4-53a10353f4a8]]. Revelation's own bio lists shows alongside [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]], [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]], [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]], [[Social Distortion|e1e05cce-3922-44e1-8f20-015abe5e309d]] and the [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]].

eras.title: Dressed nice, and made to answer for it
eras.text: Two seven-inches came out and the band became the West Coast's best argument for straight edge. They also cared how they looked, from varsity jackets and Nike high-tops to German army pants and leather Pachuco shoes, and a lot of people in hardcore had opinions about that.

years.p: The demo Ray Cappo heard at the band's first show went out as-is, because the master tape had been lost. The first press came on green vinyl.
years.xp:
It was cut at Spot Recording in Orange County. Frosty wrote most of the two-chord title track.

Frosty counts Chain as only the second West Coast band on Revelation, after [[No for an Answer|23d26104-95e2-473f-a704-ab0bcd702da3]], at a time when the label was almost entirely a New York story.

The UK got both seven-inches through First Strike Records, a Wigan label run out of a skate shop.

q: We liked to dress nice. So what?
years.h: Chain of Strength's clothes become the story
years.p: Chain of Strength dressed sharp: Stussy, mock turtlenecks, bleached and shaved heads, rolled cuffs, cribbed from Boston's SS Decontrol and [[DYS|f012c04d-96ca-47dd-9359-3bb11fed88b5]]. Critics called it fashion; Frosty shrugged it off.
years.xp: Chris Bratton later said the straight edge look was as codified as any Mod ensemble.

years.h: Live at Fender's Ballroom, Long Beach CA, August 4, 1989
yt: Live at Fender's Ballroom, Long Beach CA, August 4, 1989

years.h: Chain of Strength's What Holds Us Apart 7" · Foundation No. 1
years.p: Not on Revelation this time: Ryan Hoffman's own label, Foundation, launches with it. Gang vocals come from a crowd of scene friends, and the songs turn toward betrayal inside hardcore itself.

years.h: Chain of Strength breaks up as side projects take over
years.p: Chris Bratton is drumming for [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]] with [[Zack de la Rocha|aa659468-db56-41c9-b6fe-61f4bb2ef1a6]], and Alex Barreto, who'd drummed in Inside Out's early days, goes on to start Statue. An EP's worth of new Chain of Strength songs never gets recorded.
years.xp: Frosty has described the lost material as Subject to Change by [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]] meets [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]]'s Out of Step. The band later called the breakup kind of traumatic.

eras.title: Both records, one sleeve
eras.text: Both seven-inches had gone out of print and kids kept asking. Revelation put everything on one record and the band's catalog has been in print ever since.

years.h: Chain of Strength's The One Thing That Still Holds True
years.p: Revelation's compilation gathers True Till Death, What Holds Us Apart and one song nobody had heard, eleven tracks in all, on CD, LP and cassette. The 12" followed in 1996.

eras.title: Twenty-four years later, Irving Plaza
eras.text: Revelation's 25th birthday finally got the five of them back in a room. Two New York nights turned into Los Angeles, a Washington church and a festival in Quebec, with a new generation of bands on the same bills.

years.h: Chain of Strength reunite for Rev25 at Irving Plaza
years.p: Chain of Strength's first shows since the breakup, on Revelation's 25th anniversary weekend in New York, October 12 and 13, plus a Brooklyn show at Acheron.

years.h: Chain of Strength's first interview in 20 years: mostly clothes
years.p: Vice gets the band on record and they spend it on Nike high-tops, hooded sweatshirts and German army pants. Chris Bratton's point: you could play hardcore without a punk costume of leather and spikes.

years.h: Chain of Strength's reunion reaches Los Angeles
years.p: The Chain of Strength reunion comes home to Southern California.

years.h: Chain of Strength at St. Stephen's in DC, with [[Turnstile|7b748dac-f5ce-45a7-9b95-c1d8b5b013ed]]
years.p: A short run with [[Turnstile|7b748dac-f5ce-45a7-9b95-c1d8b5b013ed]], [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]], Mindset and Praise: the D.C. church on June 14, Acheron in Brooklyn the next night, Anchors Up in Haverhill on June 18.

years.h: Chain of Strength at Amnesia Rockfest, Quebec
years.p: Chain of Strength on a festival poster with [[Blink-182|0743b15a-3c32-48c8-ad58-cb325350befa]], [[Mötley Crüe|26f07661-e115-471d-a930-206f5c89d17c]] and [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]], in Montebello.
